text:
maria: FYI customer reported repeated 503s + timeouts when calling hosted /v1/generate since ~09:12 UTC. They say requests show as billed but no streaming response. escalating to incidents.

support-bot: New incident created INC-336789: hosted inference 5xx/timeouts, suspected authz gateway failures. Paging oncall.

oliver: I see a correlating spike from 09:10-09:18 in gateway auth-proxy: lots of upstream timeouts and 502->503 conversions. Short log sample: 
```
2026-03-17T09:11:32Z auth-proxy ERROR upstream_read_timeout user=acct-123 req=/v1/generate
2026-03-17T09:11:33Z token-refresh WARN failed to refresh token status=500 err="connection reset"
2026-03-17T09:11:33Z gateway INFO converted 401->503 for req=/v1/generate
```

emma: Repro attempt from my laptop returns 503 consistently: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"hi"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"upstream timeout","code":"UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT"}

lucas: Confirmed billing side flag: some requests reach the billing pipeline and increment usage before gateway returns upstream timeouts. That's why customer sees charges despite no response. Not ideal.

oliver: Root cause hypothesis: recent auth-proxy change (conn pool / token refresh) introduced a race where token-refresh failures are retried synchronously, blocking connection slots and causing upstream timeouts under short bursts. See diff: changed default pool_size 50->20 in deploy 09:05.

maria: Immediate mitigations?

oliver: Two short-term options: 1) revert pool_size patch to restore capacity (fast), 2) enable model-fallback on hosted gateway to a cached smaller model instance (mitigates customer impact if requests can be served degraded). I'd start with revert.

raj: I'm on rollback now. Reverting auth-proxy config to previous pool_size and re-deploying canary in eu-west. ETA ~10m. I will monitor 5xx rate and connection saturation.

sre-bot: deploybot: Revert deploy initiated by raj. Canary target: auth-proxy eu-west. Job 77421 queued.

oliver: While rollback runs, enable temporary circuit-breaker to fail fast on token-refresh errors to avoid tying up worker threads: set token_refresh_timeout=200ms and token_refresh_retries=0 for gateway. That should drop load rather than hang.

emma: I'll contact customer (Acme) support thread and offer timeline + mention rollback + degraded fallback enabled. cc @maria

support-bot: Support ticket #ACME-459 updated: customer notified of mitigation steps and ETA.

raj: Canary revert completed at 09:28. Metrics: connection_pool_used dropped from 92%->34%, 5xx rolling 1m rate down from 22%->3% in eu-west.

maria: Good. Are there any lingering errors or customers still affected?

lucas: A small subset of long-running requests still returning 503 due to billing pipeline retries; these are likely to be cleared now that gateway is healthy. We'll reconcile charges for any request that didn't finish with response.

oliver: Action items I propose: 
- oliver: create PR to add integration tests for token-refresh failure modes and connection pool saturation (owner: oliver)
- raj: add a config safeguard so pool_size cannot be lowered below 40 without a canary+load test (owner: raj)
- emma: coordinate customer follow-up + confirm refunds/credits if necessary (owner: emma)
- lucas: add billing-side detection to mark requests that incremented usage but didn't return successful response (owner: lucas)
- maria: schedule postmortem meeting and ensure notes (owner: maria)

maria: I'll create the postmortem doc and invite SRE, Eng infra, Billing and Support. Proposed time: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC.

sre-bot: Reminder: incident INC-336789 severity=P1 -> postmortem required.

oliver: Quick QA note: we should also consider an ephemeral increase to gateway connection limits during load windows until we have longer-term auto-scaling around token refresh stalls. I'll draft proposal.

raj: I'll add the pool_size safeguard and a canary-runbook to avoid accidental drops. PR up by EOD.

emma: Customer said they can confirm service is back for most calls, will request they verify full repro cases and report any remaining failures.

maria: Closing war room for now. We'll treat as active incident until postmortem completes and billing reconciliation finished. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
